title: Two-arrow fraction model for a pullback-stable denominator class
statement:
Use small ordinary categories, nerves, spaces, quasicategories and coherent functor categories as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], enlarging universes when needed. Let $\mathcal A$ be a small ordinary category. Let $W$ contain all isomorphisms and satisfy two-out-of-three. Let $T\subseteq W$ contain all isomorphisms, be closed under composition, and have pullbacks along every arrow, with the pullback arrows again in $T$. Assume that for every $w:a\to b$ in $W$ there exist $s:a\to z$, $p:z\to a$ and $r:z\to b$ with $ps=1_a$, $rs=w$, and $p,r\in T$. No functorial choices are assumed. For $x,y\in\mathcal A$ define $R_T(x,y)$ to have objects spans $x\xleftarrow{t}u\xrightarrow{f}y$ with $t\in T$ and morphisms $h:(u,t,f)\to(u',t',f')$ satisfying $t'h=t$ and $f'h=f$; such an $h$ automatically belongs to $W$.

There exist a quasicategory $\mathcal L$ and an essentially surjective functor $q:N\mathcal A\to\mathcal L$ inverting $W$, with the following two properties. For every quasicategory $\mathcal E$, restriction induces an equivalence from $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal L,\mathcal E)$ onto the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(N\mathcal A,\mathcal E)$ on functors inverting $W$, retaining all coherent transformations. For each $x,y$, the weak homotopy type of $NR_T(x,y)$ is naturally equivalent to $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal L}(qx,qy)$. This equivalence is natural under postcomposition in $y$ and under functors preserving $W$ and $T$, including coherent compatibility with diagrams of target maps. It sends the component of $(t,f)$ to $q(f)q(t)^{-1}$ in $\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathcal L}(qx,qy)$; consequently every arrow from $qx$ to $qy$ is homotopic, relative to its endpoints, to such a fraction. Here $h\mathcal L$ has the same objects as $\mathcal L$ and morphism sets $\pi_0$ of its mapping spaces.
